intro: Between yes and no: agreeing with conditions, avoiding an answer, and refusing politely or flatly.
p.negarse a.consejo: The e becomes «ie»: «me niego», «te niegas». An infinitive follows: «me niego a firmar».
p.siempre que.consejo: With the subjunctive it is a condition: «siempre que vengas». With the indicative it means «cada vez que».
p.si no hay más remedio.glosa: if there is no other way
p.si no hay más remedio.consejo: It accepts something reluctantly. Here «remedio» means «solution». The h in «hay» is silent.
p.ya veremos.consejo: It often promises nothing and works as a soft «no». «Veremos» comes from «ver».
p.tendré que pensarlo.glosa: I will have to think about it
p.tendré que pensarlo.consejo: «Tendré» is the future of «tener»; «pensarlo» joins «pensar» and «lo». It helps you gain time.
p.haré todo lo posible.glosa: I will do everything I can
p.haré todo lo posible.consejo: «Haré» is the future of «hacer» and the h is silent. It often comes with «pero no te prometo nada».
p.lamentablemente.consejo: It is used before giving bad news politely. It comes from the adjective «lamentable».
p.lamentar.consejo: With «lo» it says you feel sorry: «lo lamento». It is a little more formal than «lo siento».
p.no tengo por qué.consejo: It takes an infinitive: «no tengo por qué esperar». Here «por qué» is written separately and with an accent.
p.de ninguna manera.consejo: It is a firm «no». It uses «ninguna» because «manera» is feminine. «De ningún modo» means the same.
p.no me da la gana.glosa: I do not feel like it (rude)
p.no me da la gana.consejo: It is very blunt and rude. Better not to use it with bosses or strangers.
p.rotundamente.consejo: It comes from «rotundo». It goes with «negar» or «rechazar»: «me niego rotundamente».
p.obligación.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -ción: «una obligación». You say «tengo la obligación de…».
p.insistir en.consejo: It takes «en»: «insiste en venir». With a conjugated verb: «insiste en que vengas».
b1.texto:
When someone asks you for something, Spanish gives you a whole scale.

**1. Yes, with conditions.**

- **Vale, siempre que** me lo **devuelvas** mañana.
- **Si no hay más remedio…**

**2. Neither yes nor no.**

- **Haré todo lo posible**, pero no te prometo nada.
- **Tendré que pensarlo.**
- **Ya veremos.** In Spain it very often means no.

**3. A polite no.** It needs regret and a reason.

- **Lo lamento**, pero tengo otro compromiso.
- **Lamentablemente**, ese día no estoy.

**4. A flat no.**

- **Me niego a** firmar eso. **Me niego rotundamente.**
- **No tengo por qué** hacerlo.
- **De ninguna manera.**
- **No me da la gana.** It is rude: keep it for real anger.
b2.f0.texto: Alberto, I would need you to stay until nine this evening.
b2.f1.texto: Unfortunately, today I have to pick up my daughter.
b2.f2.texto: Could you come on Saturday morning?
b2.f3.texto: I will have to think about it.
b2.f4.texto: The report has to be ready on Monday.
b2.f5.texto: If there is no other way, I will come.
b2.f6.texto: We will pay you the overtime.
b2.f7.texto: But I refuse to work on Sunday as well.
b4.texto:
These phrases ask for a specific construction:

- **Siempre que** + subjunctive = condition: **siempre que me lo devuelvas**.
- **Negarse a** + infinitive: **me niego a pagar**. The e becomes ie: me niego.
- **No tengo por qué** + infinitive: **no tengo por qué esperar**.
- **Insistir en** + infinitive or + **que** and the subjunctive: **insiste en que me quede**.

With the indicative, **siempre que** means «every time»: **siempre que llueve, me quedo en casa**.
b4.e0.texto: I will lend you the book as long as you give it back to me tomorrow.
b4.e1.texto: I refuse to pay that fine.
b4.e2.texto: I do not have to give you explanations.
b5.f0.texto: The evening light comes in through the blinds and draws golden stripes on the desks.
b5.f1.texto: Alberto looks at the clock on the wall and feels a small weight in his chest.
b5.f2.texto: On the desk, the phone vibrates with a short buzz.
b5.f3.texto: His daughter is already waiting for him at the school gate.
b5.f4.texto: When his boss insists that he stay, he slowly shakes his head.
b5.f5.texto: The boss sighs and takes off her glasses with a tired gesture.
b5.f6.texto: Neither of them raises their voice in the empty office.
b5.f7.texto: Outside, the wind moves the leaves of the tree with a soft murmur.
b5.f8.texto: Alberto picks up his coat and slowly goes out into the dark corridor.
b5.f9.texto: Behind him, the door closes with a short, firm click.
b6.o0.refuerzo: It is very blunt and rude: not polite.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: it apologises and gives a reason.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is firm and curt: a flat no, not a polite one.
b6.pregunta: Which one is a polite no?
b7.frase: Vale, siempre que me lo ____ mañana.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «siempre que» as a condition takes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: With the indicative, «siempre que» means «every time».
b7.o2.refuerzo: A condition with «siempre que» asks for the subjunctive.
b8.frase: Si no hay más remedio, lo haré yo
b8.traduccion: If there is no other way, I will do it myself
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it leaves the decision for later.
b10.o1.refuerzo: It is a firm no, without doubts.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is a very warm yes.
b10.pregunta: Which answer avoids saying yes or no?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I will do everything I can.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: It is not about knowing, but about obligation.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is not about time, but about obligation.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Yes: it says there is no obligation to do it.
b12.pregunta: What does «No tengo por qué» mean?
p.quedaras.consejo: From «quedarse», to stay somewhere. The u in «que» is silent.
p.pagaremos.consejo: Future of «pagar». The ending «-emos» means we will.
p.extra.consejo: «extra» does not change form in plural. It is the same in both genders.
p.devuelvas.consejo: «devolver» is a stem-changing verb: o becomes ue in many forms.
p.darte.consejo: The pronoun «te» attaches to the infinitive: «darte».
p.explicaciones.consejo: From «explicar». Ends in «-ción», like many Spanish nouns.
p.rayas.consejo: A line that is long and thin. The y sounds like «y» in «yes».
p.doradas.consejo: From «dorar», to gild or brown. Think of «oro» gold.
p.peso.consejo: Also means money in Spanish. Here it means a heavy feeling.
p.jefa.consejo: The j sounds like h. The feminine form of «jefe».
p.insiste.consejo: From «insistir». The stress falls on the middle syllable «sis».
p.quede.consejo: Subjunctive of «quedarse» after «que». The «u» is silent.
p.niega.consejo: From «negar». The ñ-like sound in «niega» is written ni.
p.gesto.consejo: The g before e sounds like h: «gesto» is GES-to, with the j-sound only in «gesto» before e.
p.recoge.consejo: From «recoger», to gather or pick up. The g before e sounds like h.
p.clic.consejo: A short onomatopoeia, like the sound of a button or a latch.
p.obligado.consejo: From «obligar», to force someone. «No estoy obligado» means I am not required.
p.hacerlo.consejo: «lo» attaches to the infinitive: «hacer» + «lo» = «hacerlo», to do it.
